## Introduction and Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to use core tidyverse functions (`dplyr::filter()`, `stringr::str_detect()`, `dplyr::mutate()`, `dplyr::case_when()`, `dplyr::summarize()`, `forcats::fct_reorder()`, and `ggplot2`) to wrangle and visualize New York Knicks shot-chart data loaded via `hoopR::load_nba_shots()`.

**Extension (Kevin V):** The final section, "Extension: Points per Shot and the League Comparison," builds on this analysis. It converts field-goal percentage into points per shot, compares the Knicks with the rest of the NBA zone by zone, and breaks down the shot mix of the Knicks' top scorers using `tidyr::pivot_wider()` and `tidyr::pivot_longer()`.

## Data source

For this assignment, data will be loaded from the `hoopR` package to access shot-chart data for the New York Knicks.

## Codebase

### Data loading

`hoopR::load_nba_shots()` downloads pre-scraped NBA shot events directly from public SportsDataverse releases, so no local data files are required. Here we load the complete 2025–26 NBA season (`seasons = 2026`).

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(hoopR)
```

```{r}
nba_shots <- load_nba_shots(seasons = 2026)
```

###  Filtering to New York Knicks Field-Goal Attempts

In `hoopR`'s ESPN-sourced shot data, the New York Knicks are identified by `team_abbrev == "NY"`. We use `dplyr::filter()` and `stringr::str_detect()` to isolate Knicks field-goal attempts (excluding free throws) with valid court coordinates.

```{r}
nyk_shots <- nba_shots |>
  filter(
    team_abbrev == "NY",
    !str_detect(coalesce(type_text, ""), regex("free throw", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    !is.na(coordinate_x),
    !is.na(coordinate_y),
    abs(coordinate_x) <= 47,
    abs(coordinate_y) <= 25
  )
```

### Normalizing Court Coordinates and Classifying Shot Zones

Teams switch baskets at halftime, so shots can appear on either end of the full court (`-47` to `+47` feet). Using `dplyr::mutate()` and `dplyr::case_when()`, we fold all attempts onto the left half-court (rim at `x = -41.75, y = 0`), compute shot distance in feet, and classify each attempt into basketball shot zones.

```{r}
nyk_shots_clean <- nyk_shots |>
  mutate(
    x_half = -abs(coordinate_x),
    y_half = if_else(coordinate_x > 0, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y),
    shot_distance = sqrt((x_half - (-41.75))^2 + y_half^2),
    shot_zone = case_when(
      shot_distance <= 8 ~ "Paint / Restricted Area",
      (abs(y_half) >= 22 & x_half <= -33) | shot_distance >= 23.75 ~
        if_else(abs(y_half) >= 22 & x_half <= -33, "Corner 3", "Above-the-Break 3"),
      TRUE ~ "Mid-Range"
    ),
    shot_result = if_else(scoring_play, "Made", "Missed")
  )
```

### Summarizing Shooting Efficiency by Zone

Using `dplyr::group_by()` and `dplyr::summarize()`, we calculate field-goal attempts, makes, field-goal percentage, average shot distance, and shot distribution across zones.

```{r}
nyk_zone_summary <- nyk_shots_clean |>
  group_by(shot_zone) |>
  summarize(
    attempts = n(),
    made = sum(scoring_play, na.rm = TRUE),
    fg_pct = made / attempts,
    mean_distance_ft = mean(shot_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(shot_share = attempts / sum(attempts)) |>
  arrange(desc(attempts))

nyk_zone_summary
```

### Visualizing the Knicks' Zone Efficiency

#### Field-Goal Percentage by Shot Zone

Using `forcats::fct_reorder()`, we order the shot zones by efficiency before plotting with `ggplot2`.

```{r}
nyk_zone_summary |>
  mutate(shot_zone = fct_reorder(shot_zone, fg_pct)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fg_pct, y = shot_zone, fill = shot_share)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#006BB6",
    high = "#F58426",
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "NY Knicks Field-Goal Percentage by Shot Zone\n(2025–26)",
    x = "Field-Goal Percentage (FG%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Share of FGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Extension: Points per Shot and the League Comparison

*Added by Kevin V.*

The chart above ranks zones by field-goal percentage. FG% treats every shot the same, but a made three is worth 3 points and a made two is worth 2. That means a 40% three-pointer produces more points than a 50% two-pointer. This section measures each zone by **points per shot**, compares the Knicks to the rest of the league, and looks at how the Knicks' main scorers choose their shots.

### Points per Shot by Zone

`score_value` records the points each attempt produced: 0 for a miss, and 2 or 3 for a make. Its average across a group of shots is the points per shot. Here it's added to the Knicks summary with `dplyr::left_join()`, so the original FG% columns stay in place for comparison.

```{r}
nyk_points <- nyk_shots_clean |>
  group_by(shot_zone) |>
  summarize(points_per_shot = mean(score_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

nyk_zone_summary <- nyk_zone_summary |>
  left_join(nyk_points, by = "shot_zone")

nyk_zone_summary |>
  select(shot_zone, attempts, fg_pct, points_per_shot, shot_share) |>
  arrange(desc(points_per_shot))
```

```{r}
nyk_zone_summary |>
  mutate(shot_zone = fct_reorder(shot_zone, points_per_shot)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = points_per_shot, y = shot_zone)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#006BB6", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", points_per_shot)), hjust = -0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "NY Knicks Points per Shot by Zone\n(2025–26)",
    x = "Points per shot",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

best_zone  <- nyk_zone_summary |> slice_max(points_per_shot, n = 1)
worst_zone <- nyk_zone_summary |> slice_min(points_per_shot, n = 1)
mid_range  <- nyk_zone_summary |> filter(shot_zone == "Mid-Range")
corner_3   <- nyk_zone_summary |> filter(shot_zone == "Corner 3")
```

Measured this way, the ranking changes. Mid-range jumpers go in `r scales::percent(mid_range$fg_pct, accuracy = 0.1)` of the time, more often than corner threes at `r scales::percent(corner_3$fg_pct, accuracy = 0.1)`. But a mid-range shot produces only `r sprintf("%.2f", mid_range$points_per_shot)` points per shot, compared with `r sprintf("%.2f", corner_3$points_per_shot)` for a corner three. The best zone for the Knicks is `r best_zone$shot_zone` at `r sprintf("%.2f", best_zone$points_per_shot)` points per shot, and the worst is `r worst_zone$shot_zone` at `r sprintf("%.2f", worst_zone$points_per_shot)`.

### How the Knicks Compare to the League

To compare the Knicks to the rest of the NBA, every team's shots need the same zones. Instead of copying the zone code above, I wrapped it in a function so the same rules apply to all 30 teams.

```{r}
add_shot_zones <- function(shots) {
  shots |>
    filter(
      !str_detect(coalesce(type_text, ""), regex("free throw", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      !is.na(coordinate_x),
      !is.na(coordinate_y),
      abs(coordinate_x) <= 47,
      abs(coordinate_y) <= 25
    ) |>
    mutate(
      x_half = -abs(coordinate_x),
      y_half = if_else(coordinate_x > 0, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y),
      shot_distance = sqrt((x_half - (-41.75))^2 + y_half^2),
      shot_zone = case_when(
        shot_distance <= 8 ~ "Paint / Restricted Area",
        (abs(y_half) >= 22 & x_half <= -33) | shot_distance >= 23.75 ~
          if_else(abs(y_half) >= 22 & x_half <= -33, "Corner 3", "Above-the-Break 3"),
        TRUE ~ "Mid-Range"
      )
    )
}

league_shots <- nba_shots |>
  add_count(team_abbrev, name = "team_attempts") |>
  filter(team_attempts >= 2000) |>
  add_shot_zones()

n_distinct(league_shots$team_abbrev)
```

The season data also includes the All-Star Game, where players are split into one-off teams with only a few dozen shots each. Keeping only teams with at least 2,000 shots removes those and leaves the 30 NBA teams.

```{r}
zone_comparison <- league_shots |>
  mutate(group = if_else(team_abbrev == "NY", "Knicks", "Rest of NBA")) |>
  group_by(group, shot_zone) |>
  summarize(
    attempts = n(),
    points_per_shot = mean(score_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop_last"
  ) |>
  mutate(shot_share = attempts / sum(attempts)) |>
  ungroup()

zone_comparison |>
  select(group, shot_zone, shot_share, points_per_shot) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(shot_share, points_per_shot))
```

`tidyr::pivot_wider()` turns the long table, with one row per group and zone, into a wide one with one row per zone. That puts the Knicks and league numbers side by side.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
zone_comparison |>
  mutate(shot_share = shot_share * 100) |>
  pivot_longer(c(shot_share, points_per_shot), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    measure = if_else(measure == "shot_share", "Share of all shots (%)", "Points per shot"),
    measure = fct_relevel(measure, "Share of all shots (%)"),
    shot_zone = fct_relevel(shot_zone, "Paint / Restricted Area", "Mid-Range",
                            "Corner 3", "Above-the-Break 3")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = fct_rev(shot_zone), fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Knicks" = "#F58426", "Rest of NBA" = "#9AA5B4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Knicks vs. the Rest of the NBA by Shot Zone (2025–26)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

knicks_mid <- zone_comparison |> filter(group == "Knicks", shot_zone == "Mid-Range")
league_mid <- zone_comparison |> filter(group == "Rest of NBA", shot_zone == "Mid-Range")
knicks_overall <- mean(league_shots$score_value[league_shots$team_abbrev == "NY"], na.rm = TRUE)
league_overall <- mean(league_shots$score_value[league_shots$team_abbrev != "NY"], na.rm = TRUE)
```

`tidyr::pivot_longer()` stacks the two measures into one column so `facet_wrap()` can draw them side by side. The left panel shows how often each group takes each shot, and the right panel shows how many points those shots produce.

Mid-range shots make up `r scales::percent(knicks_mid$shot_share, accuracy = 0.1)` of the Knicks' attempts, compared with `r scales::percent(league_mid$shot_share, accuracy = 0.1)` for the rest of the league. Across all zones, the Knicks score `r sprintf("%.3f", knicks_overall)` points per shot, compared with `r sprintf("%.3f", league_overall)` for the rest of the NBA.

### The Shot Mix of the Knicks' Top Scorers

The team totals hide big differences between players. This table shows where each of the six Knicks with the most attempts takes his shots, along with his points per shot.

```{r}
top_shooters <- nyk_shots_clean |>
  count(athlete_name_1, name = "attempts") |>
  slice_max(attempts, n = 6)

player_mix <- nyk_shots_clean |>
  semi_join(top_shooters, by = "athlete_name_1") |>
  group_by(athlete_name_1) |>
  mutate(points_per_shot = mean(score_value, na.rm = TRUE),
         attempts = n()) |>
  group_by(athlete_name_1, attempts, points_per_shot, shot_zone) |>
  summarize(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(share = n / attempts) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = shot_zone, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(attempts))

player_mix |>
  mutate(across(c(`Paint / Restricted Area`, `Mid-Range`, `Corner 3`, `Above-the-Break 3`),
                \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 1)),
         points_per_shot = round(points_per_shot, 2)) |>
  select(Player = athlete_name_1, Attempts = attempts, `Points per shot` = points_per_shot,
         `Paint / Restricted Area`, `Mid-Range`, `Corner 3`, `Above-the-Break 3`) |>
  knitr::kable()

most_mid <- player_mix |> slice_max(`Mid-Range`, n = 1)
```

`semi_join()` keeps only the shots taken by the six players in `top_shooters`, and `pivot_wider()` turns each player's zones into columns. `values_fill = 0` puts a 0 instead of `NA` for any zone where a player didn't take a shot.

`r most_mid$athlete_name_1` takes the largest share of his shots from mid-range, at `r scales::percent(most_mid$"Mid-Range", accuracy = 1)`. A player's points per shot depends on both his shooting and his shot selection. Mid-range shots are the least efficient zone for the team, so a player who takes a lot of them needs to make them at a high rate to keep up.

### What This Adds

- **A better measure:** Points per shot accounts for threes being worth more, so it ranks zones by how much they actually help the team score. FG% doesn't.
- **Context:** Comparing with the other 29 teams shows whether the Knicks' shot choices are typical or unusual.
- **Player detail:** The breakdown shows that the team's shot mix comes from a few players with very different styles.
- **New tidyverse tools:** `left_join()`, `add_count()`, `semi_join()`, `pivot_wider()`, `pivot_longer()`, `fct_relevel()`, and a reusable function, so the same zone rules apply to every team.
